clue.text: He's afraid of a crowd rioting

indicators.note: a crowd rioting is in disorder, so the letters of these words are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is frightened of a mob running riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rioting' is the anagram signal working on A CROWD; 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A coward is a person who lacks courage and is easily frightened.

clue.text: Randomly choose actors-plenty

parts.note: the cast is the set of actors in a play
lots means plenty

explanation.surface: A director picks performers at random from a big pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing straws or tokens to decide something leaves the choice to chance.

clue.text: Uncertain signal to arena

parts.note: a wave is a hand signal
a ring is an arena for boxing or the circus

explanation.surface: A hesitant gesture is made towards the stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wavering is hesitating or undecided.

clue.text: Fashion strong emotion

definitions.meaning: a current craze, the latest thing

explanation.definitionFit: Something all the rage is in fashion, and rage is also intense anger.

clue.text: Easy task to knock to ground

definitions.meaning: something achieved with no effort, a doddle
the verb phrase meaning to shove someone down

explanation.definitionFit: An effortless job is a pushover, and to push someone over is to knock them down.

clue.text: Not fair-client could turn nasty

parts.note: not fair in looks means ugly
a client is a customer

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper warns that a badly treated client may become aggressive.
explanation.definitionFit: An unpleasant, threatening person who may become violent is idiomatically called this.

clue.text: Start to hear wise old bird cry

indicators.note: the start of the next word means its first letter only

parts.note: the owl is traditionally the wise old bird

explanation.surface: Listening at night, one hears an owl calling.
explanation.definitionFit: A howl is a long loud cry, of a wolf or a person in pain.

clue.text: Severna little bore in the spring

indicators.note: the run of words bore the answer within them, carrying it hidden inside

explanation.surface: The tidal wave on the River Severn runs small this spring.
explanation.walkthrough: The Severn bore is a tidal surge on the River Severn in western England, strongest at spring tides; here 'bore' means carried, signalling the hidden letters in SEVERNA LITTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Vernal means of or occurring in spring, from the Latin for that season.

clue.text: Have lots of shots at cryptic puzzle

definitions.meaning: to pepper with holes from gunfire
an enigma or conundrum posed in words

explanation.definitionFit: To riddle with bullets is to fire many shots, and a riddle is a puzzling question.

clue.text: Mercilessly attack wise man about Bible

indicators.note: the wise man is placed around the Bible, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a sage is a wise man
AV is the Authorized Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: A sage lectures about scripture and is fiercely attacked.
explanation.definitionFit: To savage is to maul or criticise without mercy, a strong synonym for attacking.

clue.text: Eastern hemisphere only in ancient globe

parts.note: ancient means old
the globe is the world

explanation.surface: The eastern half of the planet appears only on an antique globe.
explanation.definitionFit: Europe, Asia and Africa, the eastern hemisphere, were known as the Old World before the Americas were reached.

clue.text: Paradise is in the sky? My word!

definitions.meaning: read literally, the abode of the blessed sits overhead

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an old-fashioned cry of astonishment, and literally says that heaven lies overhead.

clue.text: For learning, look to engineers

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Someone seeking knowledge is advised to consult the engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: Lore is traditional knowledge, the body of learning handed down on a subject.

clue.text: Dishonest trader in garden material?

definitions.meaning: slang for a dealer who handles stolen goods
panels or palings put round a garden boundary

explanation.definitionFit: A receiver of stolen goods is called a fence, and fencing is a boundary material for gardens.

clue.text: Summon just about everybody

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
everybody means all

explanation.surface: An order to gather nearly everyone together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just' is a link word smoothing the surface: 'just about' reads as 'nearly' but only 'about' gives C.
explanation.definitionFit: To summon someone is to call them to come.

clue.text: Feel depressed, in bowels of ship?

parts.note: to feel a mood is to be in it
low means depressed

explanation.surface: A sailor feels gloomy down in the hold.
explanation.definitionFit: On a vessel, the lower decks and hold are described as being beneath deck.

clue.text: Gosh! No end of fun in island

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation like gosh

indicators.note: no end of means the last letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: An exclamation of delight at endless fun on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Corfu is a Greek island in the Ionian Sea.

clue.text: Single-mindedness of the Eurostar driver?

parts.note: an obsessive narrow focus, read literally as what a train driver sees going under the Channel

explanation.definitionFit: Narrow focus on one goal is often described as a blinkered, single-track outlook, and the Eurostar runs through the Channel underground passage.

clue.text: Agile lad's extraordinary help with case

indicators.note: read as extra-ordinary, out of the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive adding no letter

explanation.surface: A nimble young man gets remarkable assistance with his luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks like luggage but is a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal aid is state funding for people who cannot afford lawyers in a court action.

clue.text: Quiet walks to abattoir

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
ambles are leisurely walks

explanation.surface: Animals plod silently to the slaughterhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A shambles was originally a meat market or slaughterhouse, before meaning a mess.

clue.text: Massage, say, that Shylock wanted

definitions.meaning: a massage pummels or kneads the body, read as a beating of the skin
in The Merchant of Venice Shylock demands this as his bond from Antonio

explanation.definitionFit: Shylock's bond entitled him to a measure of Antonio's body, while a massage punningly kneads a body.

clue.text: Bird round lake is quail

indicators.note: the bird goes round the lake letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a finch is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A small bird circling a lake turns out to be a quail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quail' looks like another bird but is the verb meaning to cower.
explanation.definitionFit: To quail is to shrink back in fear, just as one may recoil or wince.

clue.text: Girl takes route to Irish county

parts.note: gal is an informal word for girl
a way is a route

explanation.surface: A young woman heads off on the road to the west of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Galway is a county on the west coast of the Republic of Ireland.

clue.text: Burden boy carries round

indicators.note: the boy carries the round letter inside him, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a lad is a boy
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A youngster lugs a heavy weight around.
explanation.definitionFit: A load is a weight carried, the same as a burden.

clue.text: Tail off right after finishing line

indicators.note: the letter for right is placed after the finishing line, so it comes second

parts.note: the tape is stretched across the finish of a race

explanation.surface: A runner fades in the final stretch just past the finish.
explanation.definitionFit: To taper is to become gradually narrower or less, like a dwindling that trails away.

clue.text: Damage limb-going to hospital

indicators.note: the limb follows the hospital letter, as if going to it, so it sits second

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital on road signs
an arm is a limb

explanation.surface: An injured arm needs treatment at hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Harm is injury or hurt, a direct synonym of damage.

clue.text: Hint-you're reading it

definitions.meaning: the solver is looking at a crossword prompt right now

explanation.definitionFit: A clue is a hint, and the words of this one are what the solver is reading.

clue.text: Little Woman's wager with Henry

definitions.note: the possessive 's stands for is: the definition is one of the Little Women

parts.note: a bet is a wager
H is short for Henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A small lady places a bet alongside a man named Henry.
explanation.definitionFit: Beth March is one of the four sisters in Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women.

clue.text: Be old now, sadly, needing fresh vigour

indicators.note: sadly signals that the words are going wrong and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Feeling aged and gloomy, someone longs for renewed energy.
explanation.definitionFit: New blood means newcomers who bring fresh energy and ideas to a group.

clue.text: Sell cure for the Three Blind Mice?

definitions.meaning: to sell goods to the public in shops

definitions.text: cure for the Three Blind Mice?
definitions.meaning: in the nursery rhyme the farmer's wife cuts off their tails, so a remedy would give them back their rear appendages

explanation.definitionFit: To sell in shops is to retail, and read as re-tail it means to give tails back.

clue.text: 1 across work gets annoyingly up one's nose

definitions.meaning: a play by the dramatist who is the answer to the first across clue, Noel Coward
pollen allergy irritates the nasal passages

explanation.walkthrough: The first across clue gives the playwright Noel Coward, and one of his comedies has this title, as well as being an allergy to pollen.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel Coward wrote a 1925 comedy of this name, and the allergy causes sneezing and nasal irritation.

clue.text: Hordes travel to this holiday island

indicators.note: hordes that travel move about, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Crowds of tourists flock to a Greek holiday isle.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodes is a Greek island in the Aegean popular with tourists.
